summary: Authz/Logic differentials probed for DVWA v1.10 at low security. Key findings: (1) Security level authorization bypass via direct cookie manipulation - the 'security' cookie directly controls the application's security posture without server-side validation, bypassing CSRF-protected form on security.php. (2) Cross-Site Request Forgery on password change at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ - accepts GET requests with no CSRF token. (3) Unauthenticated database reset via setup.php - page accessible without authentication allowing attacker to reset DB and admin credentials. (4) CSRF tokens are session-bound and cross-session reuse properly rejected. (5) No IDOR endpoints found. (6) No role-based access control separation (single admin user). (7) Combined CSRF+Command Injection chaining possible due to GET-based state-changing requests.

candidates.title: Security level authorization bypass via direct cookie manipulation
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Original cookie level: low
After directly setting security=high cookie: Security level is currently: high.
With low security cookie: SQLi returns user data (First name: admin, Surname: admin)
With high security cookie: SQL injection blocked (no results returned)
candidates.poc_hint: The 'security' cookie directly controls the application's security level without server-side validation. An attacker can change the security level by simply setting the cookie value (e.g., document.cookie='security=high') bypassing the CSRF-protected form. This affects vulnerability behavior: low allows SQL injection, high blocks it. An XSS vulnerability could be used to manipulate the security level.

candidates.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on password change at low security
candidates.proof_excerpt:
GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=test123&password_conf=test123&Change=Change -> Response: 
Password Changed.
No CSRF token present in form (has password fields: 2, has CSRF token: 0)
candidates.poc_hint: The password change form at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ uses GET method with no CSRF token. An attacker can change the admin password by tricking an authenticated user into visiting: http://127.0.0.1:8080/vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=attackerpass&password_conf=attackerpass&Change=Change

candidates.title: Database setup/reset page accessible without authentication
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Unauthenticated access: HTTP 200 - page shows 'Create / Reset Database' button
Has create_db button: 1
Setup token (no auth): ea7d08dac28331a96477b132da5cc16b
POST to create_db with extracted token redirects to /setup.php (DB reset successful)
candidates.poc_hint: The /setup.php page which can create/reset the database and reset admin credentials to 'admin//password' is accessible without any authentication. An unauthenticated attacker can reset the database and admin credentials by: (1) GET /setup.php to obtain user_token, (2) POST create_db=Create/Reset Database&user_token=EXTRACTED_TOKEN

candidates.title: CSRF token session binding - cross-session reuse rejected
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Session A token used in Session B request -> Security level remains: low (no change)
Session B token used in Session A request -> Security level remains: low (no change)
CSRF tokens are properly session-bound and cross-session replay is rejected
candidates.poc_hint: CSRF tokens on security.php are properly bound to the issuing session. A token obtained in one browser session cannot be reused in another session. This provides effective CSRF protection for the security level form.

candidates.title: Combined CSRF + Command Injection attack chain possible
candidates.proof_excerpt:
GET-based CSRF on password change confirmed (no token, GET method)
Command injection at /vulnerabilities/exec/ accepts semicolon/piped commands
Combined: CSRF can trigger command injection via GET parameters
candidates.poc_hint: Since the CSRF endpoint accepts GET requests without tokens and command injection exists at /vulnerabilities/exec/, an attacker can chain these: craft a link that triggers command execution via CSRF, e.g., which would execute commands when the victim (authenticated) visits the page.

candidates.title: Security level cookie influences vulnerability behavior
candidates.proof_excerpt:
Low security cookie: SQLi returns all user data (admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob)
High security cookie: SQLi returns no results - injection blocked
Cookie manipulation directly affects application security posture without server-side validation
candidates.poc_hint: The application reads the 'security' cookie to determine vulnerability shields. Setting the cookie to 'low' enables exploitation of vulnerabilities; setting to 'high' blocks them. Combined with XSS, an attacker can downgrade security and then exploit vulnerabilities.

facts: Unauthenticated access map: login.php (200), setup.php (200 - with DB reset), config/*.bak (200), instructions.php (200), about.php (200). All /vulnerabilities/*, security.php, phpinfo.php, ids_log.php redirect 302 -> login.php.
Security level is entirely client-controlled via 'security' cookie. Setting cookie directly changes displayed level without CSRF token validation, bypassing server-side authorization control.
CSRF tokens on security.php are session-bound - tokens from session A cannot be used in session B's requests. Cross-session replay is properly rejected.
CSRF on password change at /vulnerabilities/csrf/ uses GET method with no CSRF token. An attacker can craft a simple link to change the victim's password.

Setup page at /setup.php is fully accessible without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can reset the database and admin credentials (admin/password) by extracting the user_token from the page and POSTing.
No IDOR endpoints found - no user-specific pages (account.php, profile.php, user.php, etc.) exist to test direct object reference.
No role-based access control separation exists in DVWA - only a single 'admin' user role is available, so privilege escalation testing is not applicable.
Directory listing enabled on /dvwa/includes/, /dvwa/js/, /dvwa/css/, /external/, /docs/ - accessible without authentication.
deadends: No IDOR endpoints found: account.php, profile.php, user.php, users.php, admin.php, change_password.php all return 404
No role-based access control in DVWA - only single admin user role exists
CSRF tokens on security.php are properly session-bound; cross-session token reuse is rejected (effective CSRF protection)
Login CSRF tokens are rotated on each page refresh (mitigates token fixation)
All /vulnerabilities/* pages properly redirect unauthenticated users to login.php (302)
Session fixation via URL parameter PHPSESSID: PHP does not accept session IDs via GET
